question: 'Myopia' is also known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**near-sightedness.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Myopia' is also known as near-sightedness.**
 
• Myopia is a disease in which the patient cannot see distant objects clearly.
 
 
• In myopia, the eyeball is too long for the normal focusing power of the eye. As a result, images of distant objects appear blurred.
 
 
 
• The nearsighted (myopic) eye converges rays from a distant object in front of the retina; thus, they are diverging when they strike the retina, producing a blurry image.
 
• Myopia is a condition in which the individual can focus only on nearby objects. This is why it is called Nearsightedness.
 
• **A concave lens (minus powered)** is placed in front of a myopic eye, moving the image back to the retina and clarifying the image.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Far-sightedness:**

 
 
• Hypermetropia is a condition in which the individual can focus only on faraway objects which is why it is called longsightedness or Farsightedness.
 
• In this condition, nearby objects appear blurry as the light from them is focussed behind the retina instead of on it.
 
• It can be corrected by a convex lens (converging lens).
 
 
 
• **Presbyopia:**
 
 
• The power of accommodation of the eye decreases with ageing.
 
• People with the defect can't see nearby as well as distant objects distinctly.
 
• Thus, we can say that myopia and hypermetropia both occur simultaneously.
 
• **Causes** - (a) gradual weakening of ciliary muscles, (b) diminishing flexibility of the eye lens.
 
• It can be corrected by bi-focal lenses, in which the upper portion consists of the concave lens (facilitates distant vision) and the lower portion consists of the convex lens (facilitates near vision).
 
 
 
• **Astigmatism:**
 
 
• This is an eye defect in which a blurred image is formed on the retina.
 
• It can be corrected by using spectacles, contact lenses, or by undergoing surgery.
